title: Limit theorems for a supercritical multi-type branching process with immigration in a random environment
summary: Let $\{Z_n^i = (Z_n^i(r))_{1 \le r \le d}: n \ge 0\}$ be a supercritical $d$-type branching process in an i.i.d. environment $ξ= (ξ_0, ξ_1, \dots)$, starting from a single particle of type $i$. The offspring distribution at generation $n$ depends on the environment $ξ_n$, and we denote by $M_n = (M_n(i,j))_{1 \le i,j \le d}$ the corresponding (random) mean matrix. Recently, Grama et al. (Ann. Appl. Probab. \textbf{33}(2023) 1213-1251) extended the famous Kesten--Stigum theorem to the random environment case with $d>1$.
